attributions.surface_quote: I know one thing that never dies—judgment on each one dead.

canonical_statement: Material wealth is transient and subject to rapid, unpredictable change.

attributions.surface_quote: Such are riches, as is the twinkling of an eye.

canonical_statement: The ultimate nature of reality and the origins of sacred knowledge are inaccessible to the uninitiated.

attributions.surface_quote: If of runes thou questionest him... that he had best hold silence.

canonical_statement: The true value or essence of a phenomenon can only be judged upon its completion or final state.

canonical_statement: Human nature and worldly phenomena are inherently unstable, deceptive, and subject to unpredictable change.

attributions.surface_quote: All-powerful desire makes of the sons of men fools even of the wise.

attributions.surface_quote: The mind only knows what lies near the heart.

canonical_statement: Self-contentment is the primary condition for the psychological well-being of the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: No disease is worse to a sensible man than not to be content with himself.

canonical_statement: Human character and social efficacy are fundamentally linked to the mastery of speech and memory.

attributions.surface_quote: Of wise conduct he should be, of good memory and ready speech.

canonical_statement: The acquisition of profound knowledge necessitates active verbal engagement rather than passive silence.

attributions.surface_quote: Little got I there by silence; in many words I spoke to my advantage.

canonical_statement: The acquisition of divine wisdom requires the consumption of sacred substances or knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: Odrærer is now come up To men’s earthly dwellings.

canonical_statement: The Well of Urd serves as a focal point for observation and meditation on the nature of existence.

canonical_statement: Runes and divine discourse constitute the fundamental structure of metaphysical reality.

canonical_statement: The disclosure of one's inner mental state to another is a necessary condition for the alleviation of psychological suffering.

attributions.chapter: CHAPTER VII. THE SOURCES OF NORSE MYTHOLOGY AND INFLUENCE OF THE ASA-FAITH.
attributions.surface_quote: Care gnaws the heart, if thou to no one canst thy whole mind disclose.

canonical_statement: Human social relationships and interpersonal connections require active maintenance to prevent them from falling into neglect.

attributions.chapter: CHAPTER VII. THE SOURCES OF NORSE MYTHOLOGY AND INFLUENCE OF THE ASA-FAITH.
attributions.surface_quote: With brushwood overgrown and with high grass is the way that no one treads.

canonical_statement: The moral quality of an individual's actions and character creates a reciprocal metaphysical effect on their social and personal reality.

attributions.surface_quote: A good man will bring thee favor by his praise.

canonical_statement: Personal agency and the quality of one's own labor directly manifest as either benefit or harm to the self.

attributions.surface_quote: A shoe, if ill made, will call down evil on thee.

canonical_statement: The individual is metaphysically linked to the injuries of others, necessitating a collective responsibility for harm.

attributions.surface_quote: Wherever of injury thou knowest, regard that injury as thy own.

canonical_statement: The true identity or spiritual origin of an individual is often hidden from those who observe them.

attributions.surface_quote: Odin is the cause That I have been unable To cast off torpor.

canonical_statement: Memory and wisdom are conceptualized as substances or energies that can be transferred via ritual consumption.

canonical_statement: The natural cycles of Day and Night are personified entities worthy of invocation and reverence.

canonical_statement: The physical world is subject to manipulation through ritualized knowledge and incantations.

canonical_statement: Entities possess intelligence and wisdom derived from multiple distinct worlds or planes of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: She had intelligence from all worlds.

canonical_statement: Specific symbolic inscriptions (runes) possess the inherent power to manipulate physical elements and natural forces.

attributions.surface_quote: Brim-runes thou must know, if thou wilt have secure afloat thy sailing steeds.

canonical_statement: Celestial phenomena are governed by the active pursuit of predatory entities.

attributions.surface_quote: two wolves; the one, whose name is Skol, pursues the sun

canonical_statement: Time is a construct established by divine entities to organize the progression of years.

canonical_statement: Natural phenomena are manifestations of specific sentient beings or entities.

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies possess the capacity to influence or physically relocate human consciousness or entities from the terrestrial realm.

attributions.surface_quote: Maane... once took children from earth.

canonical_statement: The physical universe and its governing structures are products of divine construction and intentional design.

attributions.surface_quote: Fjorgyn. A personification of the earth; mother of Thor.

canonical_statement: The afterlife is a destination where the deceased reside, capable of sending objects to the living.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Nanna sent her a finger-ring from Helheim.

canonical_statement: Divine entities are subject to predetermined fates, including death in cosmic conflict.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Freyr falls in conflict with Surt in Ragnarok.

canonical_statement: Identity is fluid and can be assumed or changed by divine beings.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Gagnraade. A name assumed by Odin.

canonical_statement: The state of virginity at the time of death determines one's post-mortem role as a servant to the goddess Gefjun.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: all those who die maids become her maid-servants

canonical_statement: There exists a liminal boundary or bridge separating the realm of the living from the realm of the dead.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The bridge between the land of the living and the dead.

canonical_statement: A state of formless void or chaos preceded the creation of the world and served as the dwelling for supreme powers.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The great yawning gap, the premundane abyss, the chaos or formless void

canonical_statement: Certain entities possess an inherent nature that persists through repeated destruction and regeneration.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Gullveig is pierced and thrice burnt, and yet lives.

canonical_statement: The perception of divine realms can be experienced as a delusion or a constructed reality.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Gylfaginning, which means the Delusion of Gylfe.

canonical_statement: The progenitor of human social hierarchies is a divine entity.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Heimdal was the father and founder of the different classes of men.

canonical_statement: The afterlife realm is located within the structural foundations of the cosmic tree.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Helheim, under one of the roots of Ygdrasil.

canonical_statement: A singular vantage point exists from which all worlds in the cosmos can be observed.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Hlidskjalf, the seat of Odin, whence he looked out over all the worlds.

canonical_statement: Human existence is preserved through cataclysmic cosmic cycles.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Hodmimer’s grove, where the two human beings were preserved during Ragnarok.

canonical_statement: Individual entities can undergo death and subsequent resurrection in a regenerated world state.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Hoder returns to life in the regenerated world.

canonical_statement: The wind is a physical manifestation generated by the activity of a giant entity.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Hræsvelgr... A giant in an eagle’s plumage, who produces the wind.

canonical_statement: The mind is an entity capable of independent existence and observation.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Huginn [Mind]. One of Odin’s ravens.

canonical_statement: The gods require external substances to maintain their immortality or vitality.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Iðunn... possesses rejuvenating apples of which the gods partake.

canonical_statement: There exists a fundamental, cyclical location where divine beings assemble both at the beginning and end of cosmic eras.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Iðavöllr... where the gods first assemble... and where they assemble again after Ragnarok.

canonical_statement: Giants represent the primordial state of existence, preceding the emergence of the gods.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The giants were the earliest created beings.

canonical_statement: Humanity is preserved through cataclysmic cycles to serve as the bridge between the old and new world.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The last beings in the old and the first in the new world.

canonical_statement: Divinity contains within itself the principle of its own termination.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Loke is the end and consummation of divinity.

canonical_statement: The creative act of forming humanity is a collaborative function of multiple divine aspects.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Odin, Hæner and Loder create Ask and Embla.

canonical_statement: The physical world is a central stronghold positioned between divine realms and external chaotic forces.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The earth and mankind are represented as a stronghold besieged by the powers of evil.

canonical_statement: The universe is structured as a series of concentric domains, with the human realm at the center.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Midgard is seated in the middle of the universe, bordered by mountains and the sea.

canonical_statement: Wisdom is a resource obtained through the sacrifice of sensory perception.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Odin pawned his eye for wisdom.

canonical_statement: The death of a solar deity represents the cyclical triumph of darkness over light.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Balder’s death was also symbolical of the victory of darkness over light.

canonical_statement: The world is destined to be destroyed by fire at the end of the current cycle.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: a host of fiends, who are to appear at Ragnarok and destroy the world by fire.

canonical_statement: The afterlife includes specific regions designated for the punishment of the wicked.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: NÁSTRÖND: A place of punishment for the wicked after Ragnarok.

canonical_statement: The cosmic structure includes a nether world inhabited by entities that interact with the deceased and the world tree.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: NIÐHÖGGR: A serpent of the nether world, that tears the carcases of the dead.

canonical_statement: The universe contains distinct realms characterized by elemental states such as mist or fog, serving as a nethermost domain.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: NIFLHEIMR: The world of fog or mist; the nethermost of the rime worlds.

canonical_statement: Temporal progression is governed by three distinct metaphysical entities representing past, present, and future.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: three heavenly norns (parcæ, fates) Urd, Verdande, and Skuld (Past, Present, and Future)

canonical_statement: Individual human destiny is predetermined at the moment of birth by external metaphysical forces.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Three norns were also present at the birth of every man and cast the weird

canonical_statement: The physical world is a construct derived from the division and organization of primordial matter.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: With Vile and Ve he parcels out Ymer.

canonical_statement: Existence is defined by a cyclical process encompassing both creation and inevitable dissolution.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: rök, is the whole development from creation to dissolution

canonical_statement: Mythological figures function as personifications of natural phenomena and seasonal cycles.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Rind... personification of the hard frozen earth. Roskva... symbolizes the ripe fields.

canonical_statement: The future is an ontological category represented by a specific entity or force.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Skuld... the norn of the future.

canonical_statement: Divine names and identities are fluid and can be shared or assumed by different entities.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Sidskeg... is also a name of Odin.

canonical_statement: The term for the highest divinity shares a common etymological root across Indo-European languages, signifying a universal concept of heaven or divine power.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Properly the generic name of the highest divinity, and remains in many compounds.

canonical_statement: The preservation of the physical world and the gods is contingent upon the active intervention of a divine protector.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: without Thor and his hammer the earth would become the helpless prey of the giants.

canonical_statement: Divine symbols possess the inherent power to consecrate objects and spaces.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: Thor consecrate these runes!

canonical_statement: The past is an ontological entity personified as a norn.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: URÐR: The norn of the past, that which has been.

canonical_statement: The present is an ontological entity defined by the process of becoming.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: VERÐANDI: The norn of the present, of that which is.

canonical_statement: The physical world is constructed from the substance of a primordial being.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: VÍLI: These three sons of Bor and Bestla construct the world out of Ymer’s body.

canonical_statement: The physical world is structured as a singular, unified organism or system, represented by a world-tree.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The whole world is symbolized by this tree.

canonical_statement: The material universe was created through the transformation and division of a primordial giant's body.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: The world created out of the body of a giant.

canonical_statement: The primordial state of existence is characterized by the interaction of opposing elemental forces, specifically fire and frost.

attributions.chapter: THE ORIGINAL ICELANDIC FORM OF THE WORD IN THE VOCABULARY,
attributions.surface_quote: He was formed out of frost and fire in Ginungagap.
